package_info.package_manager: malware-as-a-service (standalone binary, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: 2.3.0 (and earlier, as referenced by IOCs from May 2021)
package_info.why_malicious: Raccoon Stealer is a credential and cryptocurrency information stealer, distributed as a malware-as-a-service platform. It is explicitly designed to exfiltrate sensitive user data, evade detection, and facilitate cybercrime. The tool includes features for credential theft, anti-analysis, bot blocking, and reporting, all of which are malicious in intent and execution.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates installed browsers, extracts stored cookies and passwords from browser credential stores, and sends this data to a command-and-control server via outbound network connections, resulting in credential and session theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated extraction and exfiltration of browser credentials and cookies is a hallmark of infostealer malware, as it enables unauthorized access to user accounts and sessions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should never access and transmit all stored browser credentials or cookies without explicit user consent and clear user-initiated action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise password managers may access browser data, but only with explicit user authorization and never exfiltrate credentials to unknown or untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Bulk extraction of browser cookies and passwords
Outbound network transmission of credential data to C2 infrastructure

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code locates and reads data from known cryptocurrency wallet files on the filesystem, then exfiltrates this information to a command-and-control server via network communication, enabling theft of cryptocurrency assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating cryptocurrency wallet data is a direct attack on user financial assets, as it allows attackers to steal funds or private keys.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not access or transmit wallet data without explicit user consent and should never send such data to untrusted remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities may access wallet files, but only with user permission and never transmit sensitive wallet data to unknown or untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Targeted access to known wallet file locations
Reading and collecting sensitive wallet data
Network exfiltration of cryptocurrency wallet contents

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code monitors for multiple accesses from the same IP address or range, blocks these IPs, and dynamically hides the admin panel interface, thereby evading automated analysis and security scanning.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Blocking IPs based on access patterns and hiding admin interfaces are common anti-analysis and anti-crawler techniques used by malware to evade detection and hinder security research.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software, especially credential management tools, rarely implements such aggressive anti-analysis measures or dynamic interface hiding.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Web applications may block abusive IPs to prevent denial-of-service, but not to conceal C2 admin panels from researchers or security tools.
key_indicators: Automated detection of repeated access from the same IP
Conditional hiding of admin or control interfaces

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code detects IP addresses associated with crawlers or bots, blocks these IPs from accessing the C2 infrastructure, and reports the detected IP addresses to the command-and-control server, enhancing evasion and operational security.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Active detection and blocking of security researchers and crawlers, combined with reporting their IPs to the C2, is a clear sign of malicious intent and operational security measures.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not attempt to evade security monitoring by blocking and reporting security-related IPs to a remote server.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some web services block known bots to prevent scraping, but not in the context of malware C2 operations or with reporting to attacker infrastructure.
key_indicators: Crawler and bot detection logic based on IP analysis
Automated blocking of identified security research IPs
Reporting of blocked IPs to remote C2 infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Initial infection and execution of the Raccoon Stealer binary on the victim's system.
Enumeration and extraction of browser credentials and cookies.
Enumeration and extraction of cryptocurrency wallet data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of wallet data to C2

attack_chain.action: Exfiltration of all collected data to command-and-control servers.
Detection and blocking of security researchers, crawlers, and automated analysis tools.

behavioral_signatures: Automated extraction of browser credentials and cookies from credential stores
Access to and reading of known cryptocurrency wallet files on disk
Network exfiltration of sensitive data to suspicious or known Raccoon Stealer C2 domains/IPs
Active detection and blocking of multiple accesses from the same IP address or range
Detection, blocking, and reporting of crawler or security research IPs to C2 infrastructure
file_indicators: Presence of Raccoon Stealer binary (hashes: e.g., 012e382049b88808e2d0b, c993ce24a57c99dd93d1, etc.)
Unusual access to browser credential stores and wallet files by unknown processes
network_indicators: Connections to telete[.]in, tttttt[.]me, telecut[.]in, tgraph[.]io, telegram[.]cat, telegram[.]services, tlgr[.]org, xn--r1a[.]click, xn--r1a[.]link, xn--r1a[.]live, xn--r1a[.]site, xn--r1a[.]website
HTTP/S requests to URLs such as hxxps://telete[.]in/jiocacossa, hxxps://tttttt[.]me/kokajakprozak
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes accessing browser credential stores and cryptocurrency wallet files, especially if followed by outbound network connections to known Raccoon Stealer C2 domains or IPs. Look for binaries matching known Raccoon Stealer hashes. Detect anti-analysis behaviors such as blocking or reporting of security research IPs. Use network security tools to flag connections to suspicious Telegram-like domains and related infrastructure. Correlate file, process, and network activity to identify coordinated credential and wallet data theft.
